title: Make it fast
description:
The starter's methods give the right answers but are O(n²). Rewrite each one to be O(n) (or O(n log n)), so that the tests with 200 000 numbers finish in time:

```java
class Fast {
    static boolean hasDuplicate(int[] a)                  // any value twice?
    static int[] twoSum(int[] sorted, int target)         // indexes {i, j}, i < j, with sorted[i] + sorted[j] == target, or null
    static int longestRun(int[] a)                        // length of the longest run of consecutive equal values
    static int countDistinct(int[] a)
}
```

For `twoSum` the array is sorted ascending; return the pair with the smallest `i` (and for that `i`, the smallest `j`).
hints: A `HashSet` answers "have I seen this before?" in O(1) on average, which turns the nested loops of `hasDuplicate` and `countDistinct` into one loop.

For `twoSum` on a sorted array, two indexes walking towards each other also work in O(n): start at both ends; if the sum is too small move the left one right, if too big move the right one left. Take care to return the pair with the smallest `i`.
